sets.notes: Every fact is tied to the verse with exact BSB quotes and references, and nothing is added. It reads like a flat study guide with no humor, repeats the 'Not this one, baker' opener, and several explanations run only two sentences, such as card 7 right and card 19 right.

Explanations stay close to the text and land some small lines, like 'The shepherd is mending, not grading.' The card 14 False explanation opens with the reaction 'Baked just right,' and card 2 drops references while the no-contraction style sounds stiff.

The quotes are accurate and usually carry references. It uses em dashes throughout ('— that is'), adds ideas like 'steadfast love pursuing him,' talks about the app ('The statement in the card is true'), and has no Papa Dorin voice at all.

Some lines are clean and quick, like 'Nobody is rushing this meal.' Almost every explanation is only one or two sentences, card 13 bed falsely says 'A bed was earlier with the green pastures,' and card 11 misquotes 'your staff' in lowercase.

It is warm, accurate and carefully quoted, and it handles the valley with care, as in 'I think this is a heavy line, and it's okay to let it be heavy.' Five explanations open with code reactions ('Baked just right,' 'Box-worthy,' 'That's a keeper!,' 'Fine work, baker!,' 'Perfect bake!').

The right-answer explanations at least name the correct phrase from the verse. Every explanation opens with a code reaction like 'Underbaked!', none has a quote or reference, card 14 is out of order, and card 11 False says 'That's a keeper!... this one's not true,' which contradicts the answer key.

It has lively, fitting jokes like 'A sheep trying to flex in a dark canyon is in big trouble.' It adds things the text doesn't say, like the rod that 'drives off the wolves,' 'rescue from the briars,' 'weary bones' and 'Gold can vanish overnight,' and the 'pop quiz' joke leans on school.

It has good everyday comparisons, like 'No invoice at the pasture gate' and the phone that finally stops buzzing. It adds outside ideas without references, such as 'Good Shepherd,' 'covenant love,' 'Hebron was a real city where David ruled' and 'test the soul to break it,' and several explanations run past five sentences.

This is the funniest set and sounds the most natural, with lines like 'Sheep don't have boots anyway' and 'not on any map the GPS knows.' No explanation carries a reference, quotes use single marks, 'Full service' echoes the Prep line, and it adds ideas like 'a slow, honored meal.'
